Agreed scope, from the Go owner (session 44b46942), which reviews the Go side:
- Base the rule on the compared value's PROVEN STATIC TYPE, not on its origin. A map, slice, field or call origin must not matter.
- The branch is not an error handler when the compared value's static type is proven AND the policy's own "error value" predicate rejects that type. Use the SAME predicate the policy applies in the positive case, so that `error`, interfaces that embed or are error, and concrete types implementing error are handled consistently.
- If the type is unproven, the branch stays open.
Find where the static type of the compared binding or expression is available structurally: binding declarations, resolution facts, or the Go adapter's type identities. Report the source with file:line. Do not use text matching.

Go review of #7470 (44b46942): #7393 approved; the #7343 part needs changes. Review details: /tmp/review-7470/review.md, counterexample /tmp/review-7470/redeclaration.go and redeclaration-go.log. The PR is at 94c5b92644 (I added a doc sentence); work on top of it.
1. P1 soundness. The container-type negative trusts navigation inference as the static type. Inference picks the latest `:=` occurrence (get_definition/go.rs ~4467-4488) and follows its right-hand side (~5473-5486, ~6387-6413), without checking whether that `:=` declared the name anew. Counterexample: `var value any; value, fresh := slice, 0; _ = fresh; value = replacement; if value != nil {}` — `value` is statically `any`, inference says Slice(int), and the branch is dropped (failure_handlers.rs ~205, ~350-356): a silent miss on a complete run. Fix: a negative proof must use the declared binding's identity and declared static type, respecting Go's rule that `:=` declares only the names new in that scope. Reuse the structured Go binding machinery; no text fallback, and never flow-inferred types for a negative. First determine whether go-to-definition of `value` there also goes to the `:=` instead of `var value any`. If so, that is a resolver defect: report it before changing resolver semantics, because it would need producer and ICFG identity decisions with the coordinator. Add a hardwon product golden (`#[hardwon("#7343: a redeclaring := made a flow-inferred type look like the static type")]`) showing that this empty body stays unknown and incomplete; use an identifier or index right-hand side, not a composite literal.
2. P2 tests and parentheses. Add golden controls: a function-local `type error` shadow (plain shape); map, array, chan and func types; unnamed structs with and without embedded fields; an alias to error; a named basic type; a pointer to a named type; interface controls. Fix explicit_type_proof so parenthesized types are stripped for every check (~513-528 strips only for struct; ~532-540 tests the original kind for chan and func), so `(chan int)` and `chan int` are handled the same way.
Then rerun the empty-handler goldens, the focused libs, Clippy, and the mux oracle case (it should still qualify; if the fix reopens any mux branch, report it with the reason). Commit with multiline messages ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. No push. Report the head and results.
